description: Patients none of whose lab records has an RA result of '-'.

a.request: Among patients none of whose laboratory records has a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-', list the 10 with the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records. Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest hematocrit first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 END) = 0 ORDER BY AVG(HCT) IS NULL, AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10;

c.request: Looking only at patients without a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-' in their lab tests, which 10 have the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records? Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Ignore missing values in the averages and don't round. Patients none of whose lab records has an RA result of '-'.
c.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-') GROUP BY ID ORDER BY avg_hct IS NULL, avg_hct DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Patients whose Laboratory records have no row with RA = '-', ranked by their average HCT across all lab records (NULLs ignored, patients with no HCT last), returning the top 10 with ID, AVG(UA), and AVG(HCT) unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory l GROUP BY l.ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN l.RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 ORDER BY (AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL), AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10;
b.raw: Patients whose Laboratory records have no row with RA = '-', ranked by their average HCT across all lab records (NULLs ignored, patients with no HCT last), returning the top 10 with ID, AVG(UA), and AVG(HCT) unrounded.

d.request: Patients for whom no Laboratory record has RA = '-' (exclude any patient with at least one such record), ranked by their average HCT across all their lab records, returning the top 10 with ID, average UA, and average HCT, descending, with patients having no HCT values last, ignoring NULLs and without rounding.
d.sql: SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-') GROUP BY l.ID ORDER BY AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL, AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10;
